q: how long will the relief last
how long does the effect stay
entries.a: That varies with the condition, how worn the joint is and what is causing the pain, which is why the diagnostic scan comes first. The consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case rather than a number that fits everyone.

It varies with the condition, the person and how worn the tissue is, so a single figure would mislead you. That is why the scan, and where needed a diagnostic block, come first: treatment follows proof of the source. The consultant gives you a realistic answer for your case.

q: how many injections will i need
will i need more than one session

The usual effects are those of any injection: soreness, swelling or bruising at the site, and sometimes temporary numbness or a short flare. Infection, bleeding or nerve injury are uncommon, and ultrasound lets the consultant see the needle throughout. Seek urgent care for fever, spreading redness or new weakness.

These procedures are generally well tolerated. They are done through a fine needle under live ultrasound, so the consultant can see the target and avoid nearby nerves and vessels. Tell the team about your health and all your medicines when you book, as some conditions change what is used.

Not always. A nerve block is usually a local anaesthetic, sometimes with a steroid. Regenerative medicine uses a concentrate from your own blood, and prolotherapy most commonly uses dextrose. If a steroid is used, people with diabetes may see a temporary rise in sugar. The consultant explains what is used and why.

Yes. Every procedure at Halcyon is done through a fine needle under image guidance, not a cut. What goes through the needle differs: a local anaesthetic block, fluid to free a nerve, your own growth factor concentrate, a prolotherapy solution, or a radiofrequency probe.

q: does the scan have x ray radiation
entries.a: Ultrasound uses sound waves, not radiation, which is one reason it suits being used in the consulting room and to guide the needle. If any other imaging is ever needed for your procedure, the consultant will explain it to you beforehand.

Ultrasound is used twice: first to find which structure is actually generating the pain, then to guide the needle exactly where it needs to go. It is done in the consulting room, so diagnosis and treatment happen in one sitting.

They show different things. MRI gives detailed pictures and reports are useful, so bring them. Ultrasound is real time, so tendons, nerves and joints can be seen as they move and the needle can be guided live. At Halcyon both are read alongside your examination.

q: do i need an mri before coming
should i get mri done first

Usually yes. Physiotherapy or a graded exercise programme is often part of the plan alongside a procedure, so the range or strength gained is kept. The consultant tells you what to do and when, and whether anything should wait for a few days.

q: will i have to take tablets forever

Tell the team when you book. Poorly controlled diabetes may mean a procedure is delayed or changed, and if a steroid is used your sugar may rise for a short while. Do not change your diabetes medicines on your own. Frozen shoulder is also more common in people with diabetes.

q: heart patient can i get treatment
entries.a: Tell the team about any heart or blood pressure problems, and every medicine you take, when you book. These can change what is used, and blood thinners in particular need planning before an injection. Do not stop anything on your own.

Tell the team about any allergy when you book and again on the day. An allergy to a solution used would rule that option out, and the consultant checks your medicines first. With regenerative medicine the concentrate comes from your own blood, so an allergy to it is not expected.

q: what do you mean by interventional
how is this different from tablets
entries.a: Interventional pain management means finding the structure causing the pain and treating it directly with a precise, image-guided procedure through a needle, such as a nerve block, radiofrequency or a regenerative injection, rather than with surgery or tablets alone.

q: what does a pain doctor do
entries.a: A pain specialist assesses long-standing pain to find where it is coming from, and treats it with medicines, image-guided procedures and rehabilitation. At Halcyon, Dr. Dasyam Pallavi, Consultant – Pain Management, assesses you and performs the ultrasound-guided procedures.

An abnormality on an MRI or X-ray is not always the source of pain. Dr. PSS Kiran, Consultant Radiologist, reads your X-ray, MRI and ultrasound alongside the examination and provides image guidance for procedures in collaboration with Dr. Pallavi, so both pictures are weighed together.

q: difference between ortho and pain doctor
entries.a: Both have a place. An orthopaedic surgeon is the right person when an operation may be needed. A pain specialist focuses on finding the source of long-standing pain and treating it without surgery, using image-guided procedures. Many people see both, and Halcyon will tell you plainly if surgery should be considered.

Four pathways, all image-guided and day care: regenerative medicine (growth factor concentrate from your own blood), radiofrequency ablation including COOLIEF cooled RF for the knee, prolotherapy, and nerve hydrodissection with nerve blocks. The scan decides which one suits you.

Twelve: knee, low back, neck and shoulder pain, sciatica, slipped disc, hip pain, sports injuries, trigeminal neuralgia, elbow, hand and wrist pain, foot and ankle pain, and cervical spondylosis. Tell me where it hurts and I can say more.

A small injection of local anaesthetic on one suspected structure. If your usual pain settles, that structure is the source and treatment follows from it; if it does not, the plan changes. In the low back and neck especially, it is what stands between a diagnosis and a guess.

A medial branch block numbs, for a while, the tiny nerves supplying a suspected facet joint in the neck or low back, under image guidance. If your usual pain settles, that joint is confirmed as the source and facet radiofrequency may follow. If not, the plan changes.

An epidural injection is placed under imaging into the epidural space at the level the scan and examination have identified. At Halcyon it is the usual treatment for a slipped disc pressing on a nerve root, and one option for sciatica. It is day care under local anaesthetic.

A transforaminal injection is placed under imaging at the opening where the irritated nerve root leaves the spine. It aims at the root that is actually irritated rather than the whole area, and is a usual treatment for sciatica and a slipped disc.

q: how does a nerve block work
entries.a: A nerve block places medicine, usually a local anaesthetic and sometimes a steroid, on or beside a specific nerve under image guidance. It is used to calm a nerve that is firing so rehabilitation can proceed, or to prove where the pain is coming from before anything else is done.

Fluid, usually saline and sometimes with local anaesthetic or dextrose, is placed under ultrasound around a trapped nerve to separate it from the tissue pressing on it. The nerve is left intact and nothing is cut; relief often begins on the table. It is often used for carpal tunnel.

A suprascapular nerve block quietens the main nerve supplying the shoulder joint, easing pain so you can move it. At Halcyon it is used for frozen shoulder and rotator cuff pain, often with hydrodilatation, and alongside a movement programme.

Hydrodilatation places fluid into the shoulder joint under guidance to stretch a capsule that has tightened, as in frozen shoulder. It is usually paired with a suprascapular block and a movement programme, so the range freed up is kept.

Radiofrequency ablation uses a precise, controlled current through a fine probe to stop a small sensory nerve carrying the pain signal. At Halcyon it is used for knee, neck, low back and trigeminal nerve pain, and only after a diagnostic block has confirmed the source.

COOLIEF is the US FDA-cleared cooled radiofrequency system Halcyon uses for knee pain. Its water-cooled probe treats a larger volume of tissue than standard radiofrequency, so the genicular nerves around the knee can be reached more completely. A diagnostic block confirms them first.

The genicular nerves carry pain signals from the knee. A genicular nerve block first confirms they are carrying your pain; if it does, COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency of those nerves can interrupt the signal. It treats the nerves, not the joint, so it does not correct deformity.

Facet radiofrequency interrupts the small medial branch nerves carrying pain from a worn facet joint in the neck or low back. It is done only after a medial branch block has confirmed that joint as the source, under local anaesthetic as day care.

Pulsed radiofrequency is not described on the site. Halcyon's radiofrequency page covers ablation for the knee, neck, low back and trigeminal nerve, after a diagnostic block. Whether a different form suits your case is a question for the consultant; call +91 77880 91092.

A small sample of your own blood is drawn, its growth factors concentrated, and placed under ultrasound exactly where a tendon, ligament or joint has worn or torn. It aims to prompt repair rather than mask pain, so improvement is usually gradual over weeks.

Halcyon uses a growth factor concentrate made from your own blood, which is closely related to PRP: both rely on growth factors carried by platelets. It is placed under ultrasound for worn or torn tendons, ligaments and joints. The consultant explains the preparation used in your case.

q: do you do stem cell therapy
entries.a: The site describes regenerative medicine at Halcyon as growth factor concentrate from your own blood. Other injections are not listed there, so please ask the team on +91 77880 91092 rather than rely on me. The consultant explains what suits the tissue the scan shows.

Prolotherapy injects a natural irritant, most commonly a concentrated dextrose solution, into a slack or weakened ligament or tendon to restart the body's repair response. It is a short course of small injections under ultrasound, with minimal downtime; soreness for a day or two is normal.

The consultants' qualifications, training and registration are on their profile pages, including Dr. Pallavi's CIPS certification from the World Institute of Pain, USA. For anything more specific about experience with your condition, ask the team on +91 77880 91092.

Knee pain is the commonest reason people come to Halcyon, usually osteoarthritis, a meniscal tear or ligament strain. The knee is scanned in the same appointment, and the answer may be COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves, a regenerative injection or prolotherapy.

Low back pain can come from the facet joints, a disc or the sacroiliac joint, and each needs a different treatment. A diagnostic block is usually done first to prove which one it is, and the treatment, such as facet radiofrequency or an epidural, follows from that answer.

Neck pain is usually related to the facet joints or a disc. A medial branch block first identifies the joint involved, and cervical facet radiofrequency treats it only if the block confirms that joint as the source. Posture and exercise usually remain part of the plan.

Most long-standing shoulder pain is frozen shoulder or a rotator cuff problem. It is scanned in the same appointment and treated with a suprascapular nerve block, hydrodilatation or a regenerative injection, usually alongside a movement programme so the range comes back.

Pain running from the back into the leg usually means a nerve root is compressed or irritated. At Halcyon it is treated with a transforaminal or epidural injection placed under imaging, aimed at the root that is actually irritated, as day care.

A slipped or herniated disc pressing on a nerve root is, in most cases at Halcyon, treated with an image-guided epidural or transforaminal injection rather than surgery, after the examination, scan and where needed a diagnostic block confirm the level.

Hip pain usually comes from a bursa on the outside of the hip, the labrum, the tendons or an arthritic joint. It is scanned in the same room and treated with an image-guided injection into the exact structure involved; the hip is deep, so guidance matters here.

Most sports injuries damage a tendon, ligament or muscle. The injury is scanned to grade the damage, then usually treated with regenerative therapy or prolotherapy so the tissue heals, alongside graded rehabilitation. Return-to-sport timing is planned with you.

q: pain on one side of face
entries.a: Trigeminal neuralgia causes sudden electric-shock pain across one side of the face, often set off by touch, chewing or talking. Medication is the usual first treatment; when it no longer controls the pain, Halcyon offers image-guided radiofrequency ablation of the affected branch, as day care.

Elbow, hand and wrist pain usually comes from an overloaded tendon, as in tennis elbow or de Quervain's, or a trapped nerve, as in carpal tunnel. These are usually treated with ultrasound-guided nerve hydrodissection or a regenerative injection, freeing or repairing the structure rather than operating.

Heel pain worst on the first steps of the morning is usually plantar fasciitis; pain at the back of the ankle is often Achilles tendinitis. Both are scanned and usually treated with prolotherapy or a regenerative injection under ultrasound, alongside stretching and footwear advice.

Cervical spondylosis is age-related wear of the neck discs and facet joints, and it shows on almost every scan after a certain age. So a medial branch block first proves the worn joints are what hurts; if it does, cervical facet radiofrequency treats them.

Knee osteoarthritis is gradual wear of the cartilage. At Halcyon it may be treated with COOLIEF cooled radiofrequency of the genicular nerves, or a regenerative injection for early to moderate wear, chosen by the scan. In advanced grade 4 arthritis with deformity, a replacement may still be right.

Meniscal tears come from a twisting injury or wear in an older knee. The knee is scanned in the same appointment, and a regenerative injection placed under ultrasound is one option where the tissue has worn or torn. A knee that locks or will not straighten should be assessed.

A strained or slack ligament that makes the knee feel loose may suit prolotherapy or a regenerative injection. A complete tear may need a different approach, so the scan and examination decide. After a fresh injury with severe swelling or deformity, go to an emergency department.

Pain around the kneecap after running is often from overuse of the tendons or the joint behind the kneecap. The knee is examined and scanned to find which structure is involved, and treatment and your return to running are planned from that.

Pain just below the kneecap in people who jump or run is often a patellar tendon overuse problem. Ultrasound grades the tendon, and a regenerative injection or prolotherapy may be used alongside a loading programme, depending on what the scan shows.

Swelling can come with arthritis, a meniscal tear or bursitis, and the scan shows which. If the knee is hot, red and swollen with fever, or swollen after a fall and you cannot bear weight, go to an emergency department instead.

Frozen shoulder is a tightened, thickened joint capsule, more common between about 40 and 60 and in people with diabetes. At Halcyon it is usually treated with a suprascapular nerve block and hydrodilatation, alongside a movement programme so the range comes back.

Rotator cuff problems range from overuse to partial tears. Ultrasound shows the tendons directly, and a worn or torn tendon may be treated with a regenerative injection, or pain eased with a suprascapular block so rehabilitation can proceed.

Impingement and bursitis happen when tendons or the bursa are pinched and inflamed on lifting the arm. Ultrasound can usually tell an inflamed bursa from a tear or a tight capsule in one sitting, and the treatment follows from what it shows.

Tennis elbow is overload and small tears in the forearm tendons at the outer elbow, painful on gripping or turning a bottle cap. At Halcyon a worn tendon is usually treated with a regenerative injection placed under ultrasound, rather than surgery.

Golfer's elbow is the same overload process as tennis elbow, on the inner side of the elbow. The tendon is scanned, and a regenerative injection under ultrasound is one of the usual options at Halcyon.

Carpal tunnel is the median nerve squeezed at the wrist, causing numbness or tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers, often at night. At Halcyon it is usually treated with nerve hydrodissection under ultrasound. The neck is checked too, as it can mimic this.

De Quervain's tenosynovitis is irritation of the tendons at the base of the thumb, common in new parents and heavy phone or keyboard users. It is scanned and usually treated with a regenerative injection or other guided treatment chosen by what the ultrasound shows.

Trigger finger is not one of the conditions named on the site. The elbow, hand and wrist page covers tennis elbow, carpal tunnel and de Quervain's. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense for you.

Plantar fasciitis typically causes sharp pain under the heel on the first steps out of bed or after sitting. At Halcyon it is scanned and usually treated with prolotherapy or a regenerative injection under ultrasound, alongside stretching and footwear advice.

A heel spur is not named separately on the site. Heel pain is usually assessed as plantar fasciitis or an Achilles problem, and the ultrasound checks the tissue and rules out other causes before any treatment is chosen.

Achilles tendinitis causes pain and stiffness at the back of the heel, often worse in the morning and after activity. It is scanned and usually treated with prolotherapy or a regenerative injection. A sudden snap with difficulty pushing off needs an emergency department.

An old sprain can leave the ankle ligaments slack and painful, which may suit prolotherapy or a regenerative injection after the scan. If you have just twisted it and cannot bear weight, it may be a fracture, so go to an emergency department instead.

q: pain low on one side of back
entries.a: Sacroiliac joint pain is often felt low on one side, where the spine meets the pelvis. At Halcyon a block aimed at that joint is done first, and the next step is explained once it has confirmed the source.

Facet joints are the small paired joints at the back of each spinal level, and they can wear with age. A medial branch block proves whether they are the source; if it does, facet radiofrequency can interrupt the nerves carrying the pain.

Disc bulges are common on scans, including in people without pain, so the scan has to match the examination. Where a bulge is pressing on a nerve root, an image-guided epidural or transforaminal injection is the usual non-surgical treatment at Halcyon.

q: legs pain on walking relieved by sitting
entries.a: Spinal stenosis is narrowing of the spinal canal or nerve exits, more common in older adults, and one cause of sciatica. The examination and scans show the level, and an image-guided injection at the irritated root is the usual option at Halcyon.

Spondylolisthesis is one vertebra slipping forward on the one below, and it can irritate a nerve root and cause sciatica. The consultant examines you and reviews your scans; if surgery should be considered, you will be told so plainly.

Piriformis syndrome is not named on the site, but buttock pain running into the leg is assessed along the same route as sciatica and low back pain: examination, scans and, where needed, a diagnostic block to prove the source.

A pinched nerve in the low back usually causes sciatica, in the neck arm pain, and at the wrist carpal tunnel. Depending on where it is, treatment may be an image-guided root injection or hydrodissection to free the nerve. Tell me where you feel it.

Tingling or numbness running below the knee suggests a nerve root in the low back is involved, which is usually assessed as sciatica. If it is getting worse quickly, your foot is weak, or you lose bladder or bowel control, go to an emergency department.

Pain, tingling or numbness running from the neck into the arm can mean a disc or narrowing is irritating a nerve root. The consultant examines you and reviews scans; an image-guided injection aimed at that root may be advised. Worsening weakness needs urgent care.

Long hours at a desk, laptop or phone with the head held forward add load to the neck. The consultant examines you to find the source; posture changes and a neck exercise programme are usually part of the plan, with a procedure only if a structure is confirmed.

Whiplash from a road accident or sudden jolt is one cause of neck pain seen at Halcyon. If the accident was recent, or you have weakness, numbness or severe pain, go to an emergency department first; lingering pain later can be assessed here.

Headaches that start at the back of the head can come from the neck, and are assessed with neck pain. A sudden, severe headache, or one with fever and a stiff neck, is different: go to an emergency department now.

q: pain lying on side of hip
entries.a: Trochanteric bursitis is an irritated cushion on the outer side of the hip, often with gluteal tendon problems, and makes lying on that side uncomfortable. It is treated with a guided injection into the bursa or tendon, chosen by what the scan shows.

An arthritic hip tends to be stiff in the morning and makes socks or shoes harder. At Halcyon it is treated with a guided injection into the joint, chosen by what the scan shows. Bring X-ray or MRI reports; they help with arthritis.

A labral tear is damage to the rim of cartilage lining the hip socket, and may cause catching or clicking in the groin. It is treated at Halcyon with a guided injection into the joint. MRI reports help, so bring them.

Muscle strains such as hamstring or calf tears are among the sports injuries seen at Halcyon. Ultrasound grades the damage, and treatment and return to sport are planned from that, alongside graded rehabilitation.

q: pain in front of leg when running
entries.a: Shin pain is not named separately on the site. Overuse injuries from running are covered under sports injuries, where the area is examined and scanned. Pain that is worsening on one spot can need checking for a stress fracture, so get it assessed.

Tendon problems, from overuse or small tears, are common at the knee, heel, shoulder and elbow. Ultrasound shows how thickened or torn the tendon is, and a regenerative injection or prolotherapy is usually used alongside a loading programme.

Nerve pain can come from a root in the spine, a trapped nerve at the wrist or elbow, or the trigeminal nerve in the face. Tell me where you feel it. Nerve blocks, hydrodissection and radiofrequency are all used, chosen by what the examination and scan show.

Long-standing pain is exactly what Halcyon focuses on. Pain that lasts is often not where it hurts, so every appointment begins with examination and ultrasound to find the source, and treatment follows from that. Bring notes of what you have already tried.

Sudden weakness in a limb, loss of bladder or bowel control, chest pain, or back pain with fever needs to be seen urgently. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

q: cannot pass urine with back pain
entries.a: Loss of bladder or bowel control, difficulty passing urine, or numbness around the genitals, buttocks or back passage with back or leg pain can mean nerves at the base of the spine are compressed. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

Sudden or worsening weakness in a leg, foot drop, sciatica in both legs or new difficulty walking needs urgent assessment, not a clinic slot. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

q: i had cancer and now back pain
back pain at night with fever
entries.a: Back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer needs to be checked urgently by a doctor, as it can rarely mean infection or something else serious. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

After a fall, accident or major injury, especially if you cannot bear weight, the limb looks deformed, or you have neck or back pain, it may be a fracture or dislocation. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

Chest pain, or sudden left shoulder or arm pain with breathlessness or sweating, can be a heart problem. Call 108 or go to the nearest emergency department now. Please do not wait for a clinic appointment.

Sudden facial drooping, slurred speech, or weakness or numbness down one side can be a stroke. Every minute counts: call 108 or go to the nearest emergency department now. This is not something for a clinic appointment.

q: headache with stiff neck and fever
entries.a: A sudden, severe headache, the worst you have had, or a headache with fever, a stiff neck, confusion or vision changes needs emergency care. Call 108 or go to the nearest emergency department now.

A hot, red, very painful swollen joint, especially with fever, or spreading redness after an injection can mean infection. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

Swelling, pain and tenderness in the calf, especially after a long journey or surgery, can be a blood clot and needs urgent checking. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

q: heard a snap in my ankle
entries.a: A sudden snap or pop at the back of the ankle with difficulty pushing off can be an Achilles rupture. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

A head injury with confusion, vomiting, drowsiness or any loss of consciousness needs emergency care. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

Neck pain with clumsy hands that are getting worse, unsteady walking or loss of balance, numbness on both sides, or bladder or bowel changes can mean pressure on the spinal cord. Please go to the nearest hospital emergency department now, or call 108 for an ambulance. This is not something to wait for a clinic appointment for.

A wound, ulcer or colour change on the foot if you have diabetes needs prompt medical attention today, not a pain clinic slot. If it is spreading, hot, or you feel unwell with fever, go to the nearest emergency department now or call 108.

Migraine is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Headaches that start at the back of the head can come from the neck, which is assessed with neck pain. A sudden severe headache needs an emergency department. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Headache on its own is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Headaches starting at the back of the head can come from the neck. A sudden, severe or new headache with other symptoms needs an emergency department. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Cancer pain is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Your oncology team is the first place to ask. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Diabetic neuropathy is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Numbness or burning in both feet that is spreading should be checked by your doctor promptly. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Fibromyalgia or pain all over the body is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Gout is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. A hot, red, swollen joint with fever needs urgent care. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Rheumatoid or other inflammatory arthritis is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. A rheumatologist usually leads its care. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Abdominal or pelvic pain is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Severe or sudden abdominal pain needs an emergency department. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Tooth or jaw joint pain is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Sudden electric-shock pain on one side of the face may be trigeminal neuralgia, which is treated here. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Upper or mid back pain on its own is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Pain spreading to the shoulder blade can come from the neck, which is covered. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.
Tailbone pain is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Pain after shingles is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

Pain after an operation is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Your surgeon should hear about new or worsening pain first. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

q: can you treat my ear pain
entries.a: That is not one of the conditions listed on the Halcyon site. Call the team on +91 77880 91092 and they can say whether an assessment makes sense, or who would be better placed to help.

You are welcome. If anything else comes up, ask away, or call the team on +91 77880 91092, Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm. I hope you feel better soon.

q: am i talking to a bot
entries.a: I am the clinic's website assistant, answering from a fixed set of answers written from the site. I cannot see your case or give a diagnosis. For anything personal, the team on +91 77880 91092 can help.
I can only answer in English here, but you can type simply and I will do my best. For a conversation in your own language, call the team on +91 77880 91092 and ask.

I cannot diagnose anyone; that needs an examination and a scan. At Halcyon the consultant examines you and scans the painful area in the same appointment. If you have sudden weakness, bladder or bowel changes, or fever, seek emergency care instead.

q: i don't know what to ask
entries.a: I can tell you about the conditions treated, the procedures, what happens on the day, the doctors, timings, location and booking. For cost, insurance or anything about your own case, the team on +91 77880 91092 is best.
